Hi Ava — great to connect yesterday. As promised, here's a short intake list so our on-prem engineering team can size the cluster and prepare the preflight runbook. If you can return the attached site intake (pinegrove-site-intake.xlsx) plus the items below by next Wednesday it will let us put together a recommended node/config map and an MOP for the first sprint.

Key items we need from your side:
- Network diagram (VLANs, upstream BGP/egress points, NAT / firewall rules) — PDF or Visio
- Rack-level inventory (switch, TOR, uplink, PDU) + power per rack
- Expected peak QPS and avg token/sec per API for the first 6 months
- Data residency & retention constraints (SLA/retention window for KV cache, logs, model artifacts)
- KMS/HSM access model and any constraints for customer-managed keys
- Who on your infra team will own host provisioning and on-site troubleshooting (name + contact)

Questions from our side to help narrow sizing:
1) Do you want single-tenant GPUs per node pool, or shared via node labels and pod affinity?
2) Preferred CNI (Calico, Cilium) and whether you require eBPF filtering on host level?
3) Any disk encryption or LVM layering requirement beyond full-disk AES?

Attachments: pinegrove-site-intake.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Next steps: once we receive the intake we will produce a 2-page preflight summary (expected node counts, storage footprint, and recommended eviction/QoS policy) and propose 2 rollout windows for the on-site delivery.

Thanks — looking forward.

Marissa / Karthik — good notes. Quick technical recommendations below (we can expand into the one-pager):

1) Node spec (initial recommended baseline for inference nodepool)
- 8x A100y (or equivalent) per rack-compatible node type, or 4x A100 if constrained by power. If customer wants to avoid noisy neighbor, provision a dedicated inference fleet: 12 nodes with 4x A100 (or 6 nodes with 8x if they prefer fewer, larger nodes).
- CPU: 48 vCPU; Memory: 384 GB; NVMe: 4 TB per node (enterprise NVMe, RAID1-like replication at application layer)
- NIC: dual 100Gbps or 2x 40Gbps with LACP; prefer 100Gb for KV throughput.

2) KV cache approach
- Hybrid: keep hot prefix cache in-memory on node (LRU) with asynchronous write-through to local NVMe for 7-day persistence. Use a lightweight replication: push daily snapshots to a small object store on-site (or to an S3 compatible bucket behind the customer's firewall) and replicate critical keys to a second node every 24 hours. This avoids strong consistency needs while meeting audit window requirements.
- Backup cadence: daily snapshot + rolling 7-day retention; point-in-time restore window limited to full-day granularity.

3) Disk pressure & eviction
- Eviction trigger: 85% of NVMe used -> begin asynchronous snapshotting of least-recently-used prefixes and throttle further writes. If 92%+ sustained, gracefully shed non-essential caches (lower fidelity) and increase response time budget to avoid hard OOMs. Communicate this behavior in the SLO doc.

4) Cilium/eBPF constraints & host tuning
- Kernel: enable bpfilter and increase /proc/sys/net/bridge/bridge-nf-call-iptables where required for policy enforcement. Hugepages: reserve 1G hugepages for model runtime processes if model size > 10GB.
- sysctl: vm.swappiness=10; fs.nr_open tuned per node; net.core.rmem_max/wmem_max increased for high-throughput KV replication.

5) Other operational notes
- KMS: require a jump-host pattern to perform key rotation if customer restricts outbound controls. Document a minimal runbook for agents to rotate keys without re-provisioning pods.
- Preflight checklist: validate MTU end-to-end for NICs, validate NTP across cluster, and verify power/bottom-of-rack PDU sequencing (GPU power draw test).
